verdict: PNC grew revenue 11% to $6.6B on 15% higher net interest income from loan growth, and lower costs lifted profit to $2.1B.

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and securities, minus interest paid on deposits and borrowings — the bank's core engine, up 15% on commercial loan growth and higher yields.

segments.name: Fee income
segments.note: Fees for asset management, capital markets, cards, payments and other services — up 4% vs a year ago, but down 6% from a strong second quarter.

segments.name: Other noninterest income
segments.note: Private equity and other non-fee income — $214M, including a net negative $25M from Visa-related items.

opex.name: Personnel
opex.note: Pay and benefits for PNC's workforce — its biggest cost, $2.0B.

opex.name: Other noninterest expense
opex.note: All other running costs — $917M, including $27M of FirstBank integration costs.

takeaways.title: Interest income is the growth story
takeaways.text: Net interest income rose 15% to $4.2B as average loans grew to $372B and yields rose; the net interest margin was 2.94%. Revenue overall rose 11% to $6.6B.

takeaways.title: Costs fell and efficiency improved
takeaways.text: Noninterest expense fell 8% from the second quarter to $3.8B, taking the efficiency ratio to 57% from 60%. Excluding integration costs and significant items, expenses still fell 3%.

takeaways.title: Credit costs stayed contained
takeaways.text: The provision for credit losses was $189M. Net charge-offs were $257M, including $35M tied to moving a $1.4B student loan portfolio to held-for-sale; the allowance covers 1.42% of loans.

oneTimers: FirstBank integration costs were $36M before tax ($27M in expenses and $9M against noninterest income), and Visa-related significant items were a net negative $25M (an $11M gain on Visa shares, less $36M of Visa Class B-3 derivative adjustments). Together they cut net income by $48M, or $0.12 per share; adjusted EPS was $5.09 vs $4.97 reported.
footerNote: For a bank, the provision for credit losses plays the role of cost of revenue, and noninterest expense is the operating-expense block — the same model used for JPMorgan on this site.
